title: Topical Clobetasol Propionate for Inflammatory Hand osteoarthritis: A randomized trial versus placebo.(PROCLAME)
official: Topical Clobetasol Propionate for Inflammatory Hand osteoarthritis: A randomized trial versus placebo.(PROCLAME)
summary: Main objective: To compare the efficacy on pain intensity between topical clobetasol propionate 0.05% with a tapering regimen (twice daily for 2 weeks followed by once daily for 2 weeks) versus placebo in patients with inflammatory hand osteoarthritis
conditions: Adult patients with symptomatic and inflammatory Hand osteoarthritis HOA.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. •Age ≥ 45 years
2. •Symptomatic HOA according to the American College of Rheumatology criteria [10]
3. EVA ≥ 40/100 in the last 48 hours
4. •Presence of hand pain for at least 15 days in the last 30 days
5. •At least ≥2 symptomatic IP joint with clinical palpable synovitis at inclusion
6. •At least ≥2 IP joint with presence of moderate or major inflammation grey-scale synovitis (score 2 or 3) and/or Power Doppler signal (score ≥1) on ultrasound
7. •Informed written consent
8. •Patient affiliated to a social security scheme
9. Prior treatment failure (inadequate response or intolerance to at  least 1 recommended treatment among paracetamol, topical or  oral NSAIDs, or short course of corticosteroids)
Exclusion criteria:
1. •Isolated or predominant painful thumb-base OA (i.e., rhizarthrosis)
2. •Any new hand OA treatment within the 2 months prior to the inclusion visit (W0), including physiotherapy and provision of new hand splint.
3. •Use of opioids within the 4 weeks (or the equivalent of 5 half-lives) prior to the inclusion visit (W0)
4. •Planned hand surgery in the next 6 weeks.
5. •Use of any investigational (unlicensed) drug within the 3 months prior to the inclusion visit (W0).
6. •History of glaucoma contraindicating the use of corticosteroids.
7. •	Presence of a serious, uncontrolled concomitant cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal, hepatic, endocrine, gastrointestinal, neurological (including epilepsy) condition which, according to the investigator, makes the patient ineligible for the study.
8. •Systemic progressive infection
9. •Pregnant or breastfeeding woman
10. •Patient under legal protection measure (tutorship or curatorship) and patient deprived of freedom
11. •Patient is unable to apply the study drug on hands
12. •Other inflammatory joint disease (e.g. gout, reactive arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, seronegative spondyloarthropathy, Lyme disease)
13. •Participation in another interventional study or being in the exclusion period at the end of a previous study.
14. •Patient on AME (state medical aid)
15. •Current skin abnormality, irritation, or lesions of the hands (e.g., eczema, urticarial lesion, skin infection) contraindicating topical application
16. •Contraindication to propionate clobetasol
17. •Existence of a pain syndrome of the upper limbs, which would interfere with the monitoring of pain
18. •Fibromyalgia
19. •Use of oral, intramuscular or intra-articular or intravenous steroids, other anti-synovial agents (e.g. slow-acting anti-rheumatic drugs such as methotrexate, sulfasalazine), intra-articular hyaluronic acid to the hand joints within the 1 month prior to the inclusion visit (W0)
20. •Use of oral NSAIDs or paracetamol less than 48h before the inclusion visit (W0)
21. •Any topical treatment (corticosteroids included) on treated extremities for any indication, other than cosmetic use of creams and lotions, within the 2 weeks prior to the inclusion visit (W0).
